candidates.title: Request-Level Energy Attribution for Batched LLM Serving
candidates.abstract: Batched LLM serving improves throughput but complicates energy accounting. GPU power telemetry is aggregate, whereas sustainability reporting, chargeback, and workload analysis often require request-level energy charges. Existing inference-energy benchmarks report model-, phase-, or token-level energy, and recent carbon-accounting work motivates Shapley fairness conceptually. Neither provides measured request-level ground truth, so how far the accounting rules used in practice deviate from a fair allocation has remained unknown. We present JouleShare, an attribution framework with two components. An offline harness establishes this ground truth by replaying request subsets under vLLM with a reproducible protocol, integrating GPU power telemetry, and computing exact Shapley energy for each request. A lightweight calibration model, JCalib, then learns to predict Shapley shares from cheap request features for use at serving time. Across 16 model/workload runs, token-proportional attribution differs from exact Shapley by 0.440 normalized L1 on average under static batching and by 0.458 under continuous batching, a gap that reproduces across three data-center GPUs. JCalib reduces this error to 0.116 under static batching and 0.177 under continuous batching, below even a standalone-measurement baseline that is unavailable online, while preserving exact batch-energy efficiency. Sampled Shapley extends the measured reference to larger group sizes, where the gap persists and a single offline calibration remains the most accurate deployable rule. The results show that token attribution is not a reliable proxy for marginal energy under batched execution, and that measured Shapley ground truth can calibrate low-cost request features toward fairer attribution.
candidates.reason: バッチ化されたLLMサービングにおけるリクエスト単位のエネルギー帰属を、vLLMでの部分リプレイ実測とShapley値による正確な帰属、軽量な較正モデルJCalibによる予測で実現しており、推論基盤の計測・課金分析へ直接貢献する。

candidates.title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks
candidates.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts language models are cheap to run per token but expensive to hold in GPU memory, which drives the cost of serving them in production. One-shot expert compression shrinks them after a single calibration pass. Its two current state-of-the-art methods are REAP for expert pruning, which deletes the least salient experts, and REAM for expert merging, which merges them into the most salient ones. Both have been evaluated only on academic benchmarks. We compare the two on five multilingual production tasks of a web-hosting company, from classification to the generation of marketing HTML email templates, with two 30B-parameter models (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and the hybrid Mamba-attention Nemotron-3.5-Lightning) at 25% and 50% of experts removed and the same calibration data. Pruning wins: on the same rows, REAP is significantly better in 16 of 20 comparisons and REAM in 2. At 25%, REAP keeps 93.6% of Qwen3-30B's generative quality and REAM 62.5%, although on benchmarks the two are within a point for the same model. The damage concentrates in the output contract rather than the content: 89.8-95.2% of each significant loss on email templates comes from hard-gate failures such as invalid JSON, broken mobile layouts and runaway generation, and most failed non-English domain descriptions copy the prompt's English opening phrase. Cross-perplexity and logit divergence, two diagnostics from the REAP paper, also track production quality, as does the rate of repetition loops; n-gram diversity does not. We close with practical guidance for compressing MoE models for production.
candidates.reason: 実運用の多言語タスクでMoE LLMのエキスパート剪定（REAP）と統合（REAM）を同一キャリブレーション条件で比較し、25%削減時に剪定が生成品質の93.6%を保持する等、サービング時のGPUメモリ削減に直結するエキスパート圧縮の実証知見を示しており、MoE推論圧縮へ直接貢献する。

candidates.title: Sequence-Aware Split Heuristic to Mitigate SM Underutilization in FlashAttention-3 Low-Head-Count Decoding
candidates.abstract: The standard FlashAttention-3 heuristic exhibits a GPU occupancy bottleneck in low-head-count decoding configurations because it disables sequence splitting based on sequence length alone, underutilizing the Streaming Multiprocessors of Hopper GPUs. Our proposed sequence-aware split policy mitigates this by allowing sequence-level parallelism in low-head-count regimes, improving hardware utilization to deliver roughly a 21 to 24% improvement in decoder kernel efficiency on metadata-enabled inference paths, with no observed regressions.
candidates.reason: FlashAttention-3の低ヘッド数デコードで生じるSM遊休に対し、系列長だけでなく系列分割可否を再判定するsequence-aware splitヒューリスティクスを提案し、デコードカーネル効率を21〜24%改善したと一次要旨で確認でき、注意カーネルの推論最適化へ直接貢献する。
